registryEntry.supersedes: revision 2 (apnt-pool-v1-proof-system-registry-rev2-vectors.json: R1CS 25d3f54d..., one hashed public input over a 396-byte record, the 57-byte AES-256-GCM packet), whose Chipnet simulated-ceremony keys (task 5.1c re-run, historical-record, vk SHA-256 a82a7248...) are zero-value test evidence and never a vp for revision 3; and revision 1 (apnt-pool-v1-proof-system-registry-vectors.json: 396 public record bytes), never a vp. Revision 3 keeps revision 2's vp topology, so its serialization shape vector is byte-identical to revision 2's
registryEntry.name: gnark Groth16 on BN254
vpSerialization: vp = (*github.com/consensys/gnark/backend/groth16/bn254.VerifyingKey).WriteTo at gnark v0.16.3: compressed points, gnark-crypto flags in the top two bits of each point's first byte
|| u32be(|K|) || K[0..|K|-1] (32 each), |K| = 1 + 1 + number of BSB22 commitments
|| PublicAndCommitmentCommitted: u32be(outer) || for each: u32be(inner) || u64be(index)...
vpCovers: every verifying-key element gnark's Verify reads: alpha, beta, gamma, delta, K, the commitment topology and the Pedersen commitment keys
[beta]1 and [delta]1, which Verify does not read, because the one serialization includes them
not the proving key, the SRS or the circuit's R1CS: the key binds the circuit through K and the setup
registryEntry.publicInput: one BN254 scalar x = int_be(SHA-256(A)) mod r: SHA-256 over the 314 bytes of the action record A with no tag, the digest read big-endian, reduced mod the BN254 scalar field order r (vectors: apnt-pool-v1-action-public-input-vectors.json); every verifier derives x from A itself and never takes it from a prover
registryEntry.verification: gnark v0.16.3 groth16/bn254 Verify with the BSB22 commitment extension: Pedersen knowledge check e(C, GSigmaNeg) * e(PoK, G) = 1; commitment wire = expand_message_xmd(SHA-256, DST 'bsb22-commitment', 48 bytes) of the commitment point, reduced mod r; then the Groth16 pairing check
registryEntry.vpStatus: one vp recorded: chipnetZeroValueVp, the Chipnet simulated single-party ceremony's verifying key (task 5.1c re-run on revision 3, historical-record; historical-record), zero-value only and allowlisted by no canonical build. Every setup, including every re-run of a simulated setup after a circuit change, yields a new vp and so a new profile_id

shapeVector.label: SERIALIZATION SHAPE VECTOR, NOT A VERIFYING KEY: every point is bn254.HashToG1/G2 of a public label under DST 'APNT-POOL-v1 vp serialization shape vector, not a verifying key'. No Setup produced it; its profile_id must never be allowlisted

chipnetZeroValueVp.label: SIMULATED SINGLE-PARTY SETUP - ZERO-VALUE TEST ONLY
chipnetZeroValueVp.note: the verifying key of a simulated single-party ceremony: the project ran every contribution and could have kept the randomness, so it can forge proofs under this key. It must never guard value; a Chipnet pool deployment under it is an explicitly labelled zero-value test. Mainnet needs a permissionless multi-party ceremony. Recorded, not allowlisted: the aggregate program's canonical allowlist is task 5.4 slice 2's
